en: Awake, Romanian, from the sleep of death,
into which barbarous tyrants have sunk you,
now or never fashion yourself another fate,
to which even your cruel enemies shall bow.
Now or never let us give proofs to the world
that in these hands there still flows a Roman blood,
and that in our breasts we keep with pride a name
triumphant in battles, the name of Trajan!
Raise your broad brow and look around you,
how the brave lads stand like firs on the mountain, hundreds of thousands;
they wait only for a call and they leap like wolves into the sheepfolds,
old men, men, youths, young people, from the mountains and from the plains!
Behold, great shades, Mihai, Ștefan, Corvinus,
the Romanian nation, your great-grandchildren,
with arms bearing weapons, with your fire in their veins,
“Life in liberty or death” all cry.
You were destroyed by the malice of envy
and the blind disunion at the Milcov and the Carpathians!
But we, pierced to the soul by holy liberty,
swear that we will join hands, to be brothers for ever!
A mother widowed since Mihai the Great
asks of her sons today a helping hand,
and curses with tears in her eyes anyone at all
who in such a danger would turn traitor!
By lightning let him perish, by thunderbolt and brimstone,
whoever would draw back from the glorious place,
when the homeland or the mother, with tender heart,
shall ask that we pass through sword and fire!
Is it not enough, the yataghan of the barbarous crescent,
whose fatal wounds we still feel even today;
now the knout is thrust into our ancestral hearths,
but the Lord is our witness that alive we will not accept it [?]!
Is it not enough, despotism with all its blindness,
whose yoke we have borne for centuries like cattle;
now the cruel ones try, in their blind arrogance,
to rob us of our language, but only dead will we give it up!
Romanians from the four corners, now or never
unite in thought, unite in feeling!
Cry out to the wide world that the Danube is stolen
through intrigue and force, cunning schemings!
Priests, with the cross at the head, for the army is Christian,
its motto is liberty and its aim most holy.
Better we die in battle, in full glory,
than be slaves again in our old land!
notes: line 1.2: 'barbarii de tirani' is literally 'the barbarians of tyrants', i.e. barbarous tyrants.
line 1.3: 'croiește-ți' is 'cut out, fashion for yourself' (as a garment is cut).
line 3.1: 'cată-n giur' is the older spelling of 'caută-n jur', 'look around'.
line 3.4: 'juni' and 'tineri' both mean 'young (people)': 'juni' is the older, bookish word.
line 4.1: Mihai is Michael the Brave, Ștefan is Stephen the Great, Corvine (vocative) is Corvinus, the name of the Hunyadi (John Hunyadi or his son Matthias Corvinus; the line does not say which).
line 5.1: 'Pre voi' is the older form of 'pe voi', 'you' (object).
line 5.2: the Milcov is a river that formed the border between Wallachia and Moldavia; the Carpathians divided them from Transylvania.
line 6.2: 'mână d-ajutori' is 'a helping hand' (literally 'a hand of help').
line 6.3: 'blastămă' is the older form of 'blestemă', 'curses'.
line 8.1: 'iataganul barbarei semilune' is 'the yataghan of the barbarous crescent': the Ottoman sword.
line 8.3: 'cnuta' is the knout, the Russian whip.
line 8.4: 'vii nu oprimim' as printed; read as 'vii n-o primim' ('alive we will not accept it'). Taken as one word, 'oprimim' would be 'we oppress', which gives no sense here.
line 10.1: 'din patru unghiuri' is 'from the four corners'.
